summary: My Thai Star has a documentation suite that reflects its origin as a 2017 showcase application, not a maintained reference implementation. The foundation (Home.asciidoc, java-design.asciidoc, User-Stories.asciidoc) is reasonable in structure but riddled with critical inaccuracies. The most serious problems form a trilogy of misrepresentation: (1) Security documentation omits three production-blocking vulnerabilities found by code analysis; (2) NodeJS documentation describes a completely different stack (Express/DynamoDB vs actual NestJS/TypeORM) and incorrectly labels the active backend as deprecated; (3) Angular documentation is 7 major versions behind and omits the NgRx architecture entirely. Three test documentation files are empty TODO stubs, and the Java testing doc creates false confidence by showing a passing test run where code analysis found zero logic-layer unit tests. The Swagger API spec is on Swagger 2.0, is missing authentication definitions, the login endpoint, and contains capitalisation inconsistencies and typos. Overall documentation quality score is 4.9/10 (Poor), with accuracy at 4/10 and completeness at 4/10 driving the low overall result. Priority actions are: create SECURITY.md, rewrite NodeJS and Angular design docs, update Java testing docs to reflect actual coverage, and upgrade the Swagger spec.
